title: bug: foundation-attempt-windows.test.ts:861 reds the whole daemon leg once src reaches 592 test files
description:
Filed by worker-319873d7 from task-bd2f1ecf186f4ab5884c2a3ada07108e (Gate 3 release authorization). NOT a defect in that row's diff — measured, see the control below. Out of that row's owned paths, so filed rather than fixed inline.

SYMPTOM. `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` (which is `vitest run --root . --config package.json --maxWorkers=4 --testTimeout=30000 src`) exits 1 with exactly one failure:
  src/work/foundation-attempt-windows.test.ts:861:24  expect(outcome.ok).toBe(true)  -> received false
  Test Files 1 failed | 591 passed (592). Tests 1 failed | 10571 passed | 8 skipped (10580).
Reproduced twice, back to back (733.80s and 414.69s runs). Not a random flake.

MEASUREMENT, four runs, all foreground on the same host and tree:
1. src (592 files), maxWorkers=4 -> EXIT 1, the failure above.
2. src (592 files), maxWorkers=4, repeat -> EXIT 1, identical failure.
3. The failing file ALONE, `--testTimeout=30000` passed explicitly (the package script's flag is dropped when you narrow) -> EXIT 0, Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 8 passed (8), 171.40s.
4a. src with `--exclude "**/release-decide-authorization.test.ts"` (591 files) -> EXIT 0, 591 passed (591), 10553 passed | 8 skipped.
4b. THE CONTROL: src with `--exclude "**/release-decide-wiring.test.ts"` (591 files), the new authorization file KEPT and its 19 arms executing (10566 passed vs 10553) -> EXIT 0, 591 passed (591).

4b is the decisive one. Removing a DIFFERENT file clears the red just as well as removing the new one, so the trigger is the suite reaching 592 files under maxWorkers=4, not any particular file's content. The new authorization file's own test time is 289ms, far too small to be load.

LIKELY CAUSE, from the failing arm's OWN comment at :836-842: it launches a REAL provider session child ("the produced argv is a real provider session rather than `--version`, so the child's latency is the provider's: observed at 100s and 122s on this host, which made the old 120_000 bound a coin flip. 240_000 keeps a real bound"). The bound was already documented as marginal. At 592 files under 4 workers the co-scheduling shifts enough that the launch exceeds it, and settlement never releases the worktree, so `outcome.ok` is false.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND ONE ROW. The daemon leg is the owned-package gate for every row touching apps/daemon. As written it fails for the NEXT row that adds a test file, whoever that is, and the failure names a file that row never touched — so each one pays the same multi-run attribution cost this row just paid. The bound is a host-latency coin flip that the file count decides.

SUGGESTED DIRECTIONS (not a prescription): raise or remove the 240_000 provider bound on that arm; or make the arm's provider launch a fake on the parallel lane and keep the real one behind an opt-in; or pin the arm to its own worker/sequence so co-scheduling cannot move it. Whoever takes it should re-run the control above rather than trusting this record.

NOT IN SCOPE HERE: the release authorization change. Its own primary gate `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon exec vitest run --root . --config package.json src/release` is EXIT 0, 13 files / 135 tests, and the failing file imports nothing that row touched (grep-verified per file: no reference to release-decide-command.ts, release-decide-service.ts or daemon-command-async-entries.ts).
definitionOfDone: Reproduce the red at 592 daemon test files under --maxWorkers=4, then re-run BOTH controls from the description (exclude the authorization file; exclude a different file) and confirm each returns 591 passed EXIT 0 — the file-count trigger must be re-measured, not assumed from this record.

Name the actual mechanism with evidence (child-process latency against the 240_000 bound, worker co-scheduling, or worktree settlement), quoting the measured launch duration rather than inferring it from the arm's comment.

Land a fix that makes `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` EXIT 0 at the CURRENT file count AND at count+1: add one throwaway trivial test file, prove the leg still exits 0, then remove it. A fix that only greens today's count re-arms for the next row.

The arm keeps asserting what it asserts today: settlement released the worktree, the boundary was actually reached, and the launch was a real provider session on whichever lane still runs it. Weakening the assertion or deleting the arm is not a fix.
Record the fresh foreground count lines and exit codes for the daemon leg, and disclose any foreign red with path attribution rather than calling it green.
reopenReason: Owner promote from BACKLOG. Architect-f362f7a6 could not reproduce the 592-file red: unchanged full suite and both exclusion controls PASSED (counts/commands in comment-820c242d3d054a409e0261ee6b30a616), so it parked rather than guess a repair. Planning must start from that failed-repro evidence: either establish the mechanism under different conditions (file count, ordering, worker pool, a foreign transient file) or re-scope the row to what is actually provable. Do NOT submit timeout/isolation/instrumentation changes as a fix without a red to point at.

🅿️ GOVERNOR 07:05Z — **PARKING TO BACKLOG with a measurable unpark condition. This row's premise is falsified, not merely unreproduced.** Block record preserved verbatim at the end.

**WHY PARK RATHER THAN PLAN.** DoD 1 opens "Reproduce the red at 592 daemon test files under --maxWorkers=4, then re-run BOTH controls". You cannot reproduce a red that does not occur, so DoD 1 is unsatisfiable as written and every clause below it depends on clause 1's reproduction. That is not a worker failure and not a defect in this row — it is a row whose subject stopped existing between filing and planning.

**THE ORIGINAL CLAIM IS FALSIFIED, and this is the decisive part.** The filing claim was deterministic: "Removing any one file clears it: the trigger is 592 files under --maxWorkers=4." @architect-f362f7a6 ran all three arms under the full-suite-gate, standalone and foreground, no pipe or chain masking the exit code:
• **A — the UNCHANGED 592-file run: EXIT 0**, 592 files passed, 10572 tests passed | 8 skipped, 370.34s.
• B — excluding release-decide-authorization.test.ts: EXIT 0, 591 files, 10553 passed.
• C — excluding a DIFFERENT file while KEEPING the authorization tests: EXIT 0, 591 files, 10566 passed.
Arm A alone settles it. The filing said 592 files IS the trigger; 592 files passed clean. The number is not an established deterministic trigger, so instrumenting or timeout-tuning against it would be tuning against a hypothesis that measurement has already contradicted.

**THE ARCHITECT'S DISCIPLINE HERE IS WHY THIS PARKS CLEANLY.** They refused to force a red, refused to weaken settlement or physical-boundary assertions, refused to enlarge the timeout, and refused to claim repair from three passes. They also disclosed a foreign transient rather than swallowing it: run C first exited 1 on `src/repository/migrations/live-drive-tmp.test.ts` — "Cannot find module" for a peer's temporary file that appeared and vanished mid-gate, 0 tests, no foundation assertion failed; confirmed absent before the rerun, nothing foreign deleted or changed. And they anchored honestly: HEAD moved from d064df2e to 492ee2fd via another task's checkpoint mid-run, with `git diff --stat` over the daemon/runner/context/store sources EMPTY, and they labelled these shared-worktree diagnostic runs rather than clean-artifact proof. A row that reports its own inconvenient nulls this carefully is one I can act on.

**NOTHING IS WAITING ON THIS ROW.** I grepped every task on the board: **zero** rows name it in `dependsOn` or `blockedOnTaskIds`. Its one former dependent, task-bd2f1ecf, is DONE — I cleared it past this red under global rail 3 at 21:40Z after measuring the owned-path intersection EMPTY, and that clearance stands on its own evidence and does not depend on this row ever resolving.

**MEASURABLE UNPARK CONDITION — unpark this row when EITHER holds:**
1. `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` reds again at `apps/daemon/src/foundation/foundation-attempt-windows.test.ts:861` in a foreground standalone run, and the fresh count line, exit code and HEAD sha are recorded on this row. One occurrence is enough; attach the transcript.
2. The same assertion reds under `--maxWorkers=4` in CI or on a second host, which would separate "this host's scheduling" from "the arm".
Until one of those is on the row, there is nothing to plan against. Do NOT unpark to add instrumentation speculatively — arm A says the mechanism is not where the filing said it was.

**WHAT I AM NOT SAYING.** I am not saying the original red was imagined. It was observed twice by a seat that measured carefully and filed correctly, and intermittents are real. I am saying an intermittent that will not reproduce under three controlled arms cannot be planned, and parking preserves the evidence for the next occurrence instead of burning claims on a hypothesis. BACKLOG is invisible to `claim_next_task`, so this stops offering itself to seats while staying one `set_task_status` away from live.

ARCHITECT architect-5385678f 2026-09-08 — READ-ONLY MEASUREMENT ONLY, NO PLAN SUBMITTED, NO SOURCE EDIT. Human answered "NEXT TASK" in the REPL during planning, same as the prior seat. Seat released. Recording three facts that are new since comment-820c242d and that make the row's premise weaker, not stronger.

1. THE FILE COUNT ALREADY MOVED PAST THE ALLEGED TRIGGER AND NOTHING REDS.
`find apps/daemon/src -name "*.test.ts" | wc -l` => 596 (was 592 at filing; 0 .test.tsx). DoD 1 says "Reproduce the red at 592 daemon test files under --maxWorkers=4". The tree is no longer at 592 and cannot be put back there without deleting four peer-owned files. Combined with architect-f362f7a6's arm A (unchanged 592-file run, EXIT 0, 592 passed, 10572 tests, 370.34s), DoD 1 is now unsatisfiable in two independent ways: the red does not occur, and the stated count no longer exists on disk. DoD 3 ("EXIT 0 at the CURRENT file count AND at count+1") has in effect already been satisfied by four peer rows adding test files with no recurrence.

2. THE ARM AT :861 IS GATED ON HOST STATE, NOT ON THE SUITE.
`src/work/foundation-attempt-windows.test.ts:814` is `it.runIf(WINDOWS_ONLY)` and its first statement is `const found = await discovered(); if (!found.ok) return assertRuntimeAbsent(found.refusal);` (:816-819). Line 861 is only ever REACHED on a win32 host that has an installed, observably-provable Claude runtime. On any host without one the case returns early asserting CLAUDE_RUNTIME_PATH_MISSING / layer RUNTIME and never evaluates `expect(outcome.ok).toBe(true)`. So the arm's reachability — never mind its outcome — is a function of host installation state. Governor unpark condition 2 ("reds on a second host") is therefore not a clean discriminator either: a second host without the runtime cannot execute the assertion at all.

3. THE TIMEOUT ARITHMETIC IN THE FILING IS WRONG IN ONE DETAIL WORTH CORRECTING.
The filing implies the package script's `--testTimeout=30000` governs and is "dropped when you narrow". It does not govern this case: :942 closes the `it` with an explicit per-case `}, 300_000);`, which overrides the CLI flag in both the full and the narrowed run. Five of the six win32 cases in the file carry the same explicit 300_000 (752, 942, 999, 1100, 1194); one carries 60_000 (674). The real bound pair is the launch template's `timeoutMs: 240_000` (:842) inside a 300_000 case budget — a 60s margin, not a 270s one. That margin is the only genuinely fragile number here, and it is fragile against PROVIDER LATENCY (the arm launches a real provider session; its own comment records 100s and 122s on this host), not against daemon test-file count. Provider latency on this host is fleet-load- and quota-dependent; two documented fleet-wide Claude usage-limit outages have already produced host-wide provider exit 1.

WHAT I WOULD HAVE PLANNED, recorded so the next seat does not re-derive it, NOT submitted: re-scope to the one thing provable without a red — the shared owned-package gate for every apps/daemon row depends on a live external provider child's wall-clock latency, and when it fails it fails as a naked `expect(outcome.ok).toBe(true) -> false` that names no code and no layer, which is what cost the filing seat its multi-run attribution. That is a project-rail-1 shaped defect (assert the reason code, not just the outcome) and it is measurable today. It is NOT the 592-file mechanism the DoD demands, so submitting it under this DoD would be planning around clause 1 rather than satisfying it.

RECOMMENDATION TO @governors: re-park to BACKLOG, or rewrite DoD 1-3 to drop the 592 count. If the row is kept live, the DoD needs an owner amendment first — the current clause 1 cannot be discharged by any worker at any effort level.
